title: Bunk Johnson's sweet tone and later career
summary: Bunk's sweet style, how he imitated Bolden, and how Bill Russell revived him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I wondered how did Bunk Johnson play when you first heard him over there? What kind of a tone or style did he have?

Bunk never was a rough corner player. He never was rock. Bunk always a sweet corner player. A musical player. He played as much corner as he used to drink. I was supposed to lick the head too. Bunk was a nice fella.
I liked him a lot. Nice easy going.

Always was a nice easy going fella. And Bunk could play sweet. All of them tried to imitate Buddy Bowling. That's where Bunk got that style following Buddy Bowling with this sweetness. Bunk had a sweet and lovely tone. He never was rough. He never could play loud and rough like Buddy Bowling. But when Bunk left and went back home and he joined that band out there in New Iberia, well people had to have forgot about him. Until Mr. Bill Russell picked him up and took him there and made something, you know, brought him back in light again. And he put him on the top shelf and Bunk come back down home again. And when I saw Bunk again, he was in New Iberia, sick.
